strategy.summary: Reproduce the nanskew/nankurt low-variance bug in pandas by building the buggy commit dab2f73b0b61 and running the developer's new test_low_variance cases in pandas/tests/test_nanops.py, which compare nanops.nanskew/nankurt on tiny-scale (about 1e-10 and 1e-5) zero-padded arrays against scipy.stats skew/kurtosis with bias=False. On the buggy revision the fixed absolute 1e-14 zeroing threshold (_zero_out_fperr) distorts m2/m3/m4 and the result disagrees with scipy; on the fixed revision the eps-scaled tolerance lets the values through and they match.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: scipy is needed by the test via pytest.importorskip('scipy.stats'); no version is documented or era-pinned in the evidence, so the current release is chosen and this is an unverified choice
numpy, python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython have no documented or era-inferred constraint; the strategy uses current releases compatible with the checked-out pandas build, which is an unverified choice

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/test_nanops.py::TestnanskewWithBottleneck-or-TestnankurtWithBottleneck-style class methods named test_low_variance (parametrized over initial_data in {[-2.05191341e-05,-4.10391103e-05],[-2.05191341e-10,-4.10391103e-10]} and nobs in {27,10000}), added by the PR in the nanskew and nankurt test classes
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision dab2f73b0b61 the test_low_variance cases for nanskew and nankurt fail with an AssertionError from tm.assert_almost_equal because nanops returns a value that differs from scipy.stats.skew/kurtosis(bias=False) (the tiny-scale values were zeroed by the fixed 1e-14 threshold); on the fixed revision the same test IDs pass, with test_constant_series also passing after its change to tm.assert_equal.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare nanops.nanskew(data) and nanops.nankurt(data) with st.skew/st.kurtosis(data, bias=False) for data = zeros(nobs) with the first two entries set to -2.05191341e-10, -4.10391103e-10, nobs=27.

input_output_examples.input: data = np.zeros(27); data[:2] = [-2.05191341e-10, -4.10391103e-10]; nanops.nanskew(data) versus scipy.stats.skew(data, bias=False)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: nanops value disagrees with scipy because the 1e-14 absolute threshold zeroes m2/m3
input_output_examples.expected_output: nanops value matches scipy.stats.skew(data, bias=False) to assert_almost_equal precision

input_output_examples.input: st.kurtosis(data, bias=False) reference for the PR test data (from the PR description)

risks: The defect is tied to the magnitude of the data (about 1e-10 to 1e-5) relative to the absolute 1e-14 threshold, so it should reproduce on any platform, but the scipy version is undocumented and the exact floating-point result could differ slightly across numpy/scipy builds.
The test depends on scipy being importable; if scipy is absent, pytest.importorskip skips the test and it neither fails nor passes, so scipy must be installed for the transition to be observed.
The evidence does not state a numerical separation threshold between correct and incorrect answers; the transition relies on tm.assert_almost_equal's default tolerance.
Building pandas from source needs a working C/C++ toolchain and Cython; a platform or compiler difference could change build success but not the numerical behaviour itself.
The PR's new tests reference GH#57972 while the issue is #62946; the link between them is an era-inferred association not confirmed by the documented dependency constraints.

oracle.why: The developer test compares pandas output to scipy with the library's default almost-equal tolerance; scipy is the external reference named in both the test and the issue.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision nanops.nanskew/nankurt zero m2/m3/m4 because they fall below the fixed 1e-14 absolute threshold, so the returned value differs from scipy.stats.skew/kurtosis(bias=False) and tm.assert_almost_equal raises AssertionError for the tiny-scale parametrizations.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the eps-scaled tolerance (eps*max_abs raised to the 2nd/3rd/4th power times count) no longer zeroes the genuine small moments, so nanops matches scipy and the test_low_variance cases pass; test_constant_series passes with tm.assert_equal.
